directions.title: Run chronos ambient-noise clock-drift QC across the Bransfield ZX OBS array
directions.rationale: BRA05's clock was fixed with a single hand-derived −0.167 s offset, and the precision of GrowClust/hypoDD relative relocations is ultimately limited by inter-station timing. Chronos already detects sub-sample clock drift from ambient-noise cross-correlations on OBS pairs; running it across the 15-station ZX array would either validate the catalog's timing or produce per-station drift curves to apply before the earthquake-location paper.

directions.title: Measure dv/v on the timing-corrected HYS14/HYS12 records — offshore Cascadia's first single-station dv/v points
directions.rationale: Earthnote's pipeline is validated onshore across 110 broadband stations, but its scientific target — Cascadia slow slip — is best sensed offshore. COSZO has four years of clock-corrected HYS12/HYS14 data, and clock drift is exactly the error that corrupts dv/v. The corrected records are both a unique validation set for chronfix and the first offshore extension of the PNW monitoring map — especially valuable now that the installation cruise slipped to 2027 and no new offshore seismic data will arrive this year.

directions.title: Port the Bransfield OBS picking/association/location stack to the COSZO network geometry during the cruise-postponement window
directions.rationale: The COSZO installation cruise was postponed to 2027 (Revelle repairs), so there is now a full year before six-node margin data arrives — time to port and de-risk rather than scramble. BransfieldEQ has an end-to-end OBS pipeline (PhaseNet instance @ 0.1 + OBSTransformer picking, PyOcto association, NLLoc/GrowClust relocation) tuned on ocean-bottom data; standing it up against the finalized COSZO site geometry (CZSHF/CZOFF/CZOSH/CZMID plus Slope Base / Southern Hydrate Ridge) and validating on huddle-test and synthetic events means a working catalog in the first weeks of real data.

directions.title: Formalize the hand-pick vs ML catalog comparison into a methods result
directions.rationale: William asked for a hand-pick-vs-ML comparison, and Bransfield has the rare ingredients: 58,630 manual picks across 6,970 ground-truth events plus a full-year ML catalog from the same instruments. A station-by-station pick-residual and detection-completeness comparison is simultaneously a paper section and the calibration the ML catalog needs — and with the project restarted (08-27) around polarity picking, it is a natural first deliverable back to William.

directions.title: Combine the relocated Orca swarm catalog with coda-wave dv/v on the Bransfield OBS year
directions.rationale: Both the Bransfield restart (08-27) and William's 08-25 direction now converge on the Orca submarine-volcano earthquakes, and the relocated catalog already shows a verified Jan 17–18 2019 swarm onset with structural features (dike, magma chamber, asymmetric rifting). Applying Earthnote's single-station dv/v recipe to the same OBS records tests whether the swarm was accompanied by measurable velocity change — a volcanic-unrest result that pairs the fresh relocated catalog with dv/v tooling on data already in hand.

directions.title: Use the mature 4-D δβ/β inversion + checkerboard tooling to quantify what offshore COSZO stations would add to interface resolvability
directions.rationale: Tremormetry has scaled from two onshore stations to a 4-D δβ/β inversion over 12,703 LFE families / 187 stations, with checkerboard tests showing ~70–140 km resolution that is noise-limited, not geometry-limited. The postponed COSZO margin sites will eventually sit above the locked/transition zone; feeding candidate offshore station geometries into the existing checkerboard machinery now would forecast exactly how much deep-fault resolvability they add — turning station-placement into a quantitative, resolution-driven argument before 2027 deployment.

directions.title: Evaluate the OBS-domain DeepDenoiser fine-tune on COSZO huddle-test data
directions.rationale: The OBS denoiser fine-tune was built for Bransfield's noise environment and its value is still gated on the held-out August 2019 evaluation. The COSZO huddle test — now active with interns — produces collocated broadband records ideal for measuring what the denoiser does to identical real signals before trusting it on margin OBS data. The result feeds both projects' pipelines.

directions.title: Execute the Phase 2.4 frequency-band × coda-window sweep on the Tier-A pool
directions.rationale: The sweep has been scoped since April but never executed, and two open key questions hang on it: which band/coda combination maximizes correlation per station, and whether pos/neg coda sides reveal source asymmetry. With Phase 3.1 running at scale, sweeping the ~7 genuinely-usable hourly stations is cheap and would lock per-station configs before multi-year production.

directions.title: Implement the leave-one-out / even-odd-hour test to bound sub-hour clock interpolation error
directions.rationale: It is the remaining unquantified term in the chronos uncertainty budget: σ_lag and σ_model are measured, sub-hour non-linearity is not. The test was proposed in the 05-05 uncertainty work and is a contained, station-agnostic addition that would complete the error model before the toolchain ships as a standalone package.

directions.title: Quantify pressure vs current-meter coherence at collocated COSZO nodes
directions.rationale: The 06-11 action list asks for a pressure/current-meter comparison and east-node distance checks, and interns are now exploring a month of tidal-seafloor-pressure and current-meter data. A transfer-function and coherence analysis between collocated sensors would separate oceanographic signal from instrument effects in the tidal-pressure product, directly serving the calibrated-pressure Python package.

directions.title: Test Earthnote's Wiener soft-threshold denoise on chronos inter-station CCFs
directions.rationale: Phase 3.1's year-scale finding is that Wiener denoising dominates (95% of stations). Chronos's weakest case is low-SNR inter-station pairs — HYS14–HYSB1 needed a band change to 0.1–0.3 Hz to survive. Applying the same effective-K Wiener gate to chronos CCFs could recover the 1–3 Hz band on long baselines and tighten σ_lag.

directions.title: Adopt tremormetry's per-era referencing for COSZO long timeseries spanning instrument swaps
directions.rationale: Tremormetry's hardest-won lesson was that sensor and sample-rate changes create fake dv/v steps unless references are rebuilt per era — the HDW 2023 'jump' was an EHZ→HHZ artifact, and the 4-D inversion now encodes a per-family/instrument-era offset to fix exactly this. COSZO's multi-year OOI records span such instrument changes; any derived product referencing across an era boundary inherits the same artifact. Auditing era boundaries across the COSZO station set is cheap insurance.

directions.title: Port Earthnote's SNR-independent LFE waveform fingerprint to Bransfield Stage-2 tectonic-vs-icequake discrimination
directions.rationale: Earthnote built a supervised 23-feature waveform-character classifier (spectral slope, S-polarization, band fractions, envelope shape) that separates LFEs from noise and from earthquakes/blasts at ~0.97 AUC, is SNR-independent, and transfers across stations without retraining. BransfieldEQ's Stage 2 still needs a multi-class tectonic-vs-icequake discriminator; the same hand-crafted-feature-plus-autoencoder recipe is a ready-made, physically interpretable starting point for cryoseismic vs tectonic separation on the 3-component OBS data — reusing tooling instead of building a classifier from scratch.

directions.title: Complete the GPS-slip → strain → stress comparison against the 4-D δβ/β field to test whether slow slip drives deep dv/v
directions.rationale: The tremormetry program now produces a 4-D deep δβ/β movie, and the 08-19 review added a track that turns Gualandi's daily GPS slip inversion into a 31-day-smoothed strain/stress field on the same interface. Closing the loop — correlating slow-slip-driven Coulomb/stress changes against the inverted velocity-change field over ETS cycles — is the science payoff that would tell whether the deep dv/v signal is a stress proxy, and it directly exercises the adversarial-review agenda (data-gap handling, resolution-over-time, L-curve regularization).

directions.title: Build the commissioning-phase AI QA/QC dashboard: daily timing notifications + hourly spectrograms + autoencoder anomaly flags
directions.rationale: The 07-23 operations meeting committed COSZO to hybrid AI + crowdsourced QA/QC for ~450 EarthScope channels with no funded manual review, calling specifically for daily timing-issue notifications and hourly spectrograms to spot 'wonky' data. Chronos already emits daily per-station timing metrics, and Earthnote's CC.SHRK autoencoder-fingerprinting demonstrated unsupervised anomaly clustering on continuous data. Combining them into a single dashboard (timing alerts + spectrogram tiles + autoencoder outlier flags, linked from EarthScope metadata to the COSZO site) is a concrete build that satisfies the commissioning plan and could anchor the planned NSF OOI+AI proposal.
